newsitem.title: GREECE: Buyers of Greek stocks advised to be cautious.
newsitem.headline: Buyers of Greek stocks advised to be cautious.

text.p: Greek equities may be a buying opportunity after recent volatility linked to a broker's attempt to pay exchange settlement fees with bad cheques, but investors should let the dust settle before taking action, said ING Barings.
The market rose 1.37 percent Friday, taking the index to 890.39, after a 3.31 percent fall on Thursday.
"We recommend letting the dust settle before taking any action. The risk of another market interruption has subsided, but not disappeared," said an ING Barings.
The recent crisis did not change the country's fundamentals and although they are improving, there was a need of hard evidence that reforms are being implemented, the report said.
"The Athens bourse crisis highlighted the flaws in the stock market administration but it all started when the government started dealing with precisely these flaws," it said.

In ING Barings view the government was slow to react at first. It eventually reacted appropriately by injecting liquidity and introducing measures to restore short-term confidence in the system, it said.

"However, the solution was inadequate. The government did not create an automatic mechanism which will provide liquidity and guarantee settlement of past transactions when and if another local broker fails," the report said.
Based on a limited poll of 10 brokers and fund managers the market was expected to fall another 5.0 percent stabilising at around 835 points. Individual predictions ranged from 750 to 880.
